description: Du 2011 ISS pharmacy kit validation datasets V1 to V4 (space-pharmacy.md, Validation datasets).

extracted_from.section: Validation datasets: V1, V2, V3, V4
Du 2011 summary (clavulanate rate text vs Table S III-B)

vectors.description: V1. Du 2011: API content by payload, control vs flight, with fitted rates (MDP02 Tables S III-A and S III-B; cross-checked against MDP03)

inputs.conditions: Conditions: identical kits; flight on ISS from 4 July 2006; ground controls in a JSC environmental chamber; flight RH 23 to 25%, ground 36 to 44%; flight cumulative dose 110.7 mGy versus 5.45 mGy ground. Values are mean %LC (SD). "none" means no sample at that payload. Rates are linear %LC lost per 100 days with r2. Formulation, expiry and repackaging come from MDP03; MDP03 does not give them for the oral contraceptive pair. Day 13 is labeled "14 Days (P 1)" in MDP02.
inputs.parse_conventions: Day columns: 'mean (SD)' as {value, sd} in %LC; rate columns: 'rate (r2)' as {value, r2} in %LC lost per 100 days (linear); 'none' and 'not given' parse to null; USP 'n/a (set to 90 to 110 in study)' parses to {low, high, published_as_na}.

calibration_split.rule: odd row numbers (the table's # column) calibrate, even row numbers validate
calibration_split.basis: fixed by the foundation before any fit; deterministic and disjoint by construction (degradation-science.md section 8 requires calibration and validation datasets hashed and checked disjoint)
calibration_split.caution: co-formulated components straddle the split (rows 7/8 imipenem/cilastatin, 11/12 amoxicillin/clavulanate, 25/26 norethindrone/ethinyl estradiol, 35/36 sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim): they share package and storage history, so validation on these rows is not fully independent

vectors.note: Known mismatch (space-pharmacy.md, Du 2011 summary): the text gives clavulanate rates as "0.1005% and 0.0936%/100 days", but Table S III-B gives 10.1 and 9.37 %/100 days; the table values match the measured data, so the rows carry the table values. Notes: MDP03 lists atorvastatin USP range as 94.5 to 105.0 and fluconazole as 90 to 110, while MDP02 marks both "n/a" with limits "set at 90-110% for these formulations in this study". Ibuprofen and imipenem have control r2 of 0.157 and 0.021, so their rate ratios (7.02 and 9.43 in MDP06) are unreliable. Use: primary calibration of per-product first-order or zero-order rates, flight multiplier, and failure-time prediction; repackaged solids should be modeled as permeable packaging.

vectors.description: V2. Du 2011: number of formulations failing potency (MDP01 Table III; MDP02 Table S II)

inputs.parse_conventions: 'n (text)' as {value, parenthetical}; where the parenthetical gives the Table S II grid count it is also parsed as table_s_ii_grid_count.

vectors.note: Known mismatch: Table III gives 11 and 24 flight failures at payloads 2 and 4, while the Table S II grid lists 9 and 23. Assert the engine's predicted counts against the documented range, not one number (see TV-SF-2). Use: check the engine's predicted failure counts per time point.

vectors.description: V3. Du 2011: dissolution, % API dissolved at USP time point Q (MDP01 Table IV)

inputs.parse_conventions: '80 in 45' as {q_percent, minutes}; 'mean (x)' as {value, sd}. The note does not label the parenthesized number in this table; it is read as SD, as in V1 from the same paper.

vectors.note: Use: optional secondary failure mode (dissolution) for solid products.

vectors.description: V4. Du 2011: products with physical changes after flight (MDP01 Table II; "a" means returned after expiry)

inputs.parse_conventions: '(a)' suffix parsed as returned_after_expiry = true; empty cells are null. Columns are independent lists (rows do not pair products across payloads).

vectors.note: Discoloration of amoxicillin/clavulanate and liquefaction of ciprofloxacin ophthalmic ointment also occurred in payload 4 ground controls. Use: qualitative inspection flags only; physical change did not track potency.
